title: WWT Partners Weekly Briefing
description: Cisco, Dell, HPE, NetApp, F5, Intel, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, AWS, Google Cloud and VMware.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 20–27. New: Cisco opened Model Foundry at Partner Summit on Oct. 26 and described a WWT lab test of a fine-tuned Deep Network model, and AWS added ML-KEM to Key Management Service the same day. F5 and Intel items from Oct. 20 and Oct. 23 remain. VMware was quiet; the Oct. 19 NTT DOCOMO agreement was older than seven days and was removed. No new NetApp or Microsoft release was found. The Oct. 12 USFP optics note aged out.

items.headline: Cisco opens Model Foundry to partners and cites a WWT lab test of Deep Network
items.summary: Cisco said Oct. 26 at Partner Summit that Model Foundry, a service in Cisco Cloud Control, is in controlled availability for partners and can serve or fine-tune Cisco's domain models through an OpenAI-compatible API. Cisco said it tested the service with World Wide Technology and fine-tuned a 31-billion-parameter Deep Network model on troubleshooting data. WWT Chief Security Architect Naasief Edross said that fine-tune reached the right fix in 11 of 12 lab scenarios. Cisco's investor release the same day also said Cisco IQ for Partners is generally available, and the Model Foundry post names WWT in an early-access cohort for Cisco's open models.

items.headline: Cisco warns that eight eMudhra intermediate certificates can be brute-forced
items.summary: Cisco's advisory, first published Oct. 23 and updated Oct. 24, says private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates can be brute-forced in seconds because of an April 2025 key-ceremony error, and that the keys can issue fraudulent TLS certificates. Cisco says two of the CAs are for code signing and that Sectigo cross-signed all eight in May 2025. Cisco PSIRT said it is not aware of malicious use. Secure Firewall Management Center has a remediation article, while Secure Firewall ASA, Threat Defense, and Identity Services Engine were still under investigation.

items.headline: Cisco's PHP2Shell list hits Expressway and wireless backhaul, not the firewalls
items.summary: Cisco updated its PHP advisory on Oct. 23 for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which it calls PHP2Shell. Affected products are Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul, Expressway, Expressway Select, and Duo Access Gateway. Cisco says the backhaul bug requires an administrator and scores it 6.6, with a fix targeted for February 2027, while Expressway's fix is listed as 15.5.21 with the date still open and Duo Access Gateway is fixed in 3.2.0. Cisco says products not listed are not affected, including Secure Firewall ASA, Management Center, Threat Defense, IOS, IOS XE, IOS XR, and NX-OS, and that PSIRT is not aware of malicious use.

items.headline: Dell extends the AI Factory with NVIDIA from the desk to modular data centers
items.summary: At GTC Berlin on Oct. 21 Dell announced additions to the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA and said more than 6,500 enterprises have adopted it, up from 5,000 last quarter. New pieces include validated deskside agentic templates, a 64 GB Dell Pro Precision with GB10 due Oct. 23, and a Windows GB300 configuration later. In the data center, the PowerEdge M9882 puts 256 Vera CPUs in a 48U rack for agent orchestration, the air-cooled R8822 is due this month, and a modular data center reference design with NVIDIA DSX includes compute, storage, networking, rack power and liquid cooling, with availability in early 2027. Dell also said it is pairing the stack with NVIDIA's OpenShell reference architecture and Red Hat AI Factory software for agent controls.

items.headline: HPE says Private Cloud AI can mix H200 and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, and introduces a Vera CPU rack
items.summary: HPE said Oct. 21 at GTC Berlin that HPE Private Cloud AI can now combine NVIDIA H200 GPUs and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs in the same cluster, and that this support and the KAI Scheduler are generally available. HPE introduced the NVIDIA Vera CPU Rack by HPE, which it describes as 256 NVIDIA Vera CPUs with support for 22.5K sandboxes and 80 percent faster agentic CPU performance. HPE said it will support NVIDIA DSX POD and the OpenShell reference architecture, combining OpenShell on Vera, NVIDIA Sentry with BlueField-4, and Vera Rubin NVL72. API and MCP updates for Private Cloud AI are rolling out in late 2026, and a self-service developer experience is planned for 2027.

items.headline: GTC Berlin: Nemotron 3.5 models and an OpenShell reference for agents
items.summary: NVIDIA's Oct. 21 open-models post adds Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, retriever models, Kumo models for structured data, Cosmos 3.5, and Ising models for quantum computing. A separate newsroom release the same day introduces the OpenShell reference architecture for running agents with controls on what they can reach. A third post describes Confidential Bare Metal so a model builder can keep control of models and data on third-party accelerated infrastructure. Isaac's robotics expansion is covered on the Tech page.

items.headline: Palo Alto's PHP advisory, updated Oct. 26, still has PAN-OS hotfixes in flight
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory on CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 shows an update date of Oct. 26. Palo Alto says it is not aware of any malicious exploitation against its products, scores the PAN-OS issue 8.7, and says the risk is highest when the management interface is reachable from external addresses. The issue applies to PAN-OS on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama. An Oct. 25 revision said 10.2.18-h13, 11.1.16-h4, and 11.2.10-h16 had been released, while other listed hotfixes still carry estimated dates through Oct. 30; Cortex XCORE was patched Oct. 21 and WildFire Cloud on Oct. 22.

items.headline: Palo Alto lists Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense and Prisma AIRS on the OpenAI Marketplace
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks said Oct. 23 that Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense and Prisma AIRS are on the OpenAI Marketplace for OpenAI's enterprise customers. It describes Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense as an annual subscription that uses a multi-model harness, including OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber, to find and validate exposures. Palo Alto said six months of in-house testing and more than 75 customer engagements, backed by a $17 million research investment, found exposures in every assessed organization, and that more than two-thirds of exposures in third-party applications had no known CVE. Prisma AIRS is the platform it describes for discovery, runtime protection, and governance of AI applications and agents.

items.headline: Google Cloud makes an Anthropic-managed Claude deployment generally available
items.summary: Google Cloud said Oct. 23 that an Anthropic-managed option for Claude models on Google Cloud is generally available, alongside the existing Google-managed option. Google says both deliver the same frontier models on day zero, the same pricing, and Google Cloud billing, including drawdown of eligible commitments. On the Anthropic-managed option, Anthropic is the data processor under its own terms, and Claude platform features such as Managed Agents in beta are available on day zero. Google names Claude Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and Opus 5.5.

items.headline: IBM and Intel pair Sovereign Core with Trust Domain Extensions on Xeon 6
items.summary: IBM said Oct. 23 it is working with Intel to bring Intel Trust Domain Extensions on Xeon 6 processors into environments that use IBM Sovereign Core. IBM says TDX provides hardware-backed isolation for supported workloads during execution and attestation information about that environment. Intel's Anand Pashupathy said the combination is meant to extend protection through processing, not only through governance policy. IBM said the controls are complementary, and that confidential computing does not replace security architecture, access management, or compliance processes.

items.headline: F5: Telenor AI Factory will use BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes on BlueField-3
items.summary: F5 said Oct. 20 that Telenor AI Factory selected F5 BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes as an AI service plane for NVIDIA-powered sovereign AI infrastructure. F5 says the product is a Kubernetes-native control point for AI traffic, tenant isolation, telemetry, and policy, and that the data plane runs on NVIDIA BlueField-3 so those functions stay off the host CPU. Telenor AI Factory CEO Kaaren Hilsen said the point is to govern how AI services run, not only where the infrastructure sits. F5 said token-aware governance and inference traffic optimization are planned, not shipping in this release.

items.headline: AWS Key Management Service adds the NIST ML-KEM post-quantum algorithm
items.summary: AWS said Oct. 26 that Key Management Service now supports ML-KEM, the Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism in NIST FIPS 203, which AWS says is meant to replace classical Diffie-Hellman and RSA key transport against a harvest-now, decrypt-later attack. Customers can use ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768 or ML-KEM-1024. AWS says the private key is held in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 hardware security modules and that the public key can be exported for local encapsulation with libraries such as AWS-LC, OpenSSL or Bouncy Castle. The feature is not available in the Middle East (UAE), Middle East (Bahrain) or China regions.
